thin.what is missing: The 1842 gain (confidence 1) is the largest move in the dossier (about 95,000 km2: from the 40 km Monrovia core to Cliopatria's 1848 outline without Maryland County). The page says only 'By 1842, four out of the aforementioned five colonies were incorporated into Liberia'; which colonies, when, and how far inland are unknown, and the hinterland to 8.5 N is a bridging reading.

1822-1841 is a fixed 40 km radius for twenty years, but the History page says 'The first colony on Cape Mesurado was extended along the coast as well as inland' and 'In 1838 the former four settlements came together to create the Commonwealth of Liberia'; /ledger/1 records the 1838/1839 merger only as a rename. Cliopatria (inside its US rows) draws growth 29 -> 93 -> 192 -> 284 -> 501 cells 1822-1840. Dated gains for 1838/1839 (Bassa Cove and the merged settlements) and for Sinoe would replace the single 1842 jump.

1903 gain of the Parrot's Beak (confidence 1): the page says only the Mano boundary 'was then extended further northwards by mutual agreement in June 1903'; whether that gave Liberia the Beak, and from whom, is not on the page.
No gain for the 'territories east the Mano river' Liberia received in January 1911 in exchange for the Beak (no extent on the page).

No loss to the British side before 1911, although the Liberia page says British pressure 'led to a loss of Liberia's claims to extensive territories' and 'Both Sierra Leone and the Ivory Coast annexed territories' (late 19th century, undated); the author's notes overlook this sentence. Cliopatria never draws the coast west of the Mano as Liberian, so no keyframe is affected; a claim-loss event (Gallinas coast, treaty of 11 November 1885) needs a page.

Zones empty although ground changed hands: the war's own outcome quotes 'By September 1990, Doe's forces controlled only a small area'. Contest events and a rebel dossier for the NPFL ('Greater Liberia', 1990-1997) are needed.
Zones empty; LURD and MODEL held much of the country 2002-2003; contest events needed.

The 1892-1907 northern strip (and /ledger/7's 1907 loss) is Cliopatria's own 1848-minus-1885 fringe (largest piece lon -10.5..-9.37, lat 7.95..8.58, next to Sierra Leone's north-east, consistent with the Sierra Leone page's 'ceding a sizeable strip of territory to France ... shortened the Liberia-Sierra Leone boundary'); extent unverified, confidence 2 is right.
